newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish names economy, interior ministers.
newsitem.headline: Polish names economy, interior ministers.

text.p: Liberal Wieslaw Kaczmarek was appointed on Friday to head Poland's new Ministry of the Economy from January 1.
Cabinet chief-of-staff Leszek Miller, also of the former communist Democratic Left Alliance, was named to head the powerful new Ministry of the Interior and Administration.

Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz announced his choices for the posts on Thursday and PAP news agency said President Aleksander Kwasniewski had formalised the appointments as part of a cabinet reorganisation taking place on New Year's Day.
Kaczmarek, a former minister of privatisation and one of the most reform-minded leaders in Democratic Left, will now be in charge of industrial and foreign trade policy.

Since the privatisation ministry was abolished he has been deputy minister in the Treasury, which inherited the task of selling state assets. The Treasury portfolio has been promised to the coalition's junior partner, the Polish Peasant Party.
Kwasniewski appointed the current interior minister, Zbigniew Siemiatkowski, as minister without portfolio in charge of the security service.
